purpose: Adds role-based static HTML cache variants for logged-in users, with an enable/disable toggle and role selector in the admin dashboard, so logged-in users receive cached pages keyed by role group instead of falling through to full WordPress boot each request.
riskRationale: The implementation is architecturally sound with correct cache invalidation and clean separation of concerns. However, the deterministic role hash (plain md5 of role names without a site secret) creates a cookie-forgery vector that could leak admin bar content. The feature is opt-in, limiting blast radius.
breakingChanges: New advanced-cache.php layout extracts wppo_serve_cache_file() helper — sites with customized drop-ins will be overwritten on plugin upgrade (existing DROPIN_MARKER guard prevents overwriting foreign drop-ins)
New wppo_role_hash cookie may increase request size for logged-in users by ~32 bytes
Old cache variants (non-role-hashed) remain valid for visitors — no breaking change for existing cached pages

text: Well-designed role-based cache variant system that integrates cleanly with the existing caching stack. Cache invalidation correctly purges role-variant files alongside standard cache files, and the React UI follows existing component conventions. One important security issue (deterministic role hash enabling cookie forgery) and one important maintainability issue (duplicated hash logic) need resolution before merge.

reasoning: The deterministic role hash using plain md5 without a site secret allows attackers to forge the wppo_role_hash cookie and receive cached pages intended for higher-privileged roles. Fix is straightforward: include wp_salt() in the hash computation and centralise the logic into a shared utility.

message: delete_role_variant_files() is correctly called alongside every existing delete_cache_files() call in invalidate_dynamic_static_html() and clear_cache(), ensuring cache invalidation always removes role-specific files alongside standard cache files.

Extracting wppo_serve_cache_file() into a shared helper eliminates duplicated ETag/Last-Modified/304-handling logic that previously existed in the old single-branch code, making the logged-in and visitor serving paths identical and reducing the maintenance surface.

The wppo_role_hash cookie is sanitized with a strict hex-only regex filter before being used to construct the file path, preventing directory traversal or file inclusion attacks via a forged cookie value.

is_cache_allowed_for_current_user() provides a clean layered access check that respects the legacy non-logged-in default while adding role-based filtering — the logic flow (not-logged-in, setting-off, no-roles-selected, per-role-gate) is clear and testable.

should_optimise_for_logged_in() provides a clean single-gate method that all front-end optimisation hooks (defer, delay, minify, used-CSS, Google Fonts) can reference, preventing scattered is_user_logged_in() checks throughout the code.

The saveLoggedInCacheSettings callback mutates wppoSettings.settings.cache_settings from the API response, keeping the client-side global synchronized with server state — consistent with the codebase conventions.
Conditional rendering of role checkboxes only when the toggle is enabled prevents confusion when the feature is off.

The role hash is computed as substr(md5(implode(',', $roles)), 0, 12) without any site-specific secret. Since role names (e.g., 'administrator', 'subscriber') are public and md5 is deterministic, an attacker can forge the wppo_role_hash cookie to match any role, causing advanced-cache.php to serve cached pages generated by users in that role. The same vulnerable computation exists in Cache::get_logged_in_role_hash() (class-cache.php:233) and Main::set_role_hash_cookie() (class-main.php:265).
suggestion: Include a site-specific secret (e.g., wp_salt() or NONCE_KEY) in the hash computation in both locations. For the advanced-cache.php drop-in, embed the same salt value during generation in Advanced_Cache_Handler::create().

message: The role hash computation logic is duplicated between Cache::get_logged_in_role_hash() (class-cache.php:233) and Main::set_role_hash_cookie() (class-main.php:257). Both independently compute substr(md5(implode(',', $roles)), 0, 12). If one changes without the other, the cookie value and cache file name will diverge, causing cache misses for all logged-in users. This also means the security fix (adding a salt) must be applied in two places.
suggestion: Extract the role hash computation into a shared static utility method (e.g., Util::get_role_hash()) that both callers reference, ensuring algorithm consistency.

message: The wppo_role_hash cookie is never cleared on logout. While functionally harmless (the cookie is only read when the WordPress login cookie is also present), it persists role-group information in the browser beyond the session.
suggestion: Clear the cookie on logout by hooking wp_logout: call setcookie('wppo_role_hash', '', time() - YEAR_IN_SECONDS, COOKIEPATH, COOKIE_DOMAIN, is_ssl(), true).

message: The cookie is set on every init invocation including admin pages, AJAX handlers, and REST API requests, adding unnecessary Set-Cookie headers to non-front-end responses.
suggestion: Guard with !wp_doing_ajax() && !defined('REST_REQUEST') or only set on non-admin front-end requests via !is_admin().

message: The regex /^index-[a-f0-9]{12}\.html(\.gz)?$/i uses the case-insensitive flag but the hash is always lowercase hex, making the regex unnecessarily permissive.
suggestion: Drop the i flag to match only lowercase hex.

message: delete_role_variant_files() iterates all files in a directory via dirlist() and checks each with a regex. On deeply nested cache directories with thousands of files this could be slow.
suggestion: Add a file-count bail-out (e.g., process at most 500 files) or switch to a glob-based approach to prevent runaway iteration on unexpectedly large directories.

message: The WooCommerce exclusion regex matches URLs containing 'cart', 'checkout', or 'my-account' as substrings (e.g. '/cartoons/', '/checkout-test/'). This pre-existing issue now also affects logged-in cache users.
suggestion: Anchor the patterns with word boundaries or require a leading '/': preg_match('#^/(?:cart|checkout|my-account)(?:/|$)#i', $request_uri).
